beats.text: Belle Gunness was a widow with a farm in LaPorte, Indiana. Many men who answered her ads were never seen again.
beats.credit: Photo: Bain Collection, Library of Congress

beats.text: She placed ads in marriage columns, many in Norwegian-language papers.
beats.label: THE FARM ON McCLUNG ROAD

beats.text: One ad attributed to her sought a gentleman equally well provided, with a view of joining fortunes.
beats.label: THE AD
beats.credit: HistoryNet; La Porte County Historical Society

beats.text: Men came from across the Midwest, many with their savings.
beats.label: THE SUITORS
beats.credit: La Porte County Historical Society; Mental Floss

beats.text: On April 28, 1908, the farmhouse burned. The three children in her care died, and a woman was found in the ruins. Was it Belle?
beats.label: APRIL 28, 1908

beats.text: Then searchers dug in the yard. At least a dozen people were buried there. Two were identified as men who had answered her ads. Most were never named.
beats.label: MAY 1908

beats.text: Her hired man, Ray Lamphere, was convicted of setting the fire. No one was ever convicted of the murders.
beats.label: THE TRIAL, 1908

beats.text: For years, people said they'd seen her. A DNA test in 2008 couldn't settle it. LaPorte still doesn't know if Belle died in that fire.
beats.label: STILL UNSOLVED

beats.text: Did Belle get away? Tell us in the comments.
